summary: CRT handle-close helper: resolves the OS handle for CRT index a1, skips CloseHandle for the shared stdout/stderr pair (indices 1 and 2 when they map to the same OS handle) and for invalid handles, clears the handle open-state byte in the block tracking array, and maps a CloseHandle failure to CRT errno via ErrorIDLookupTable, returning 0 on success or -1 on failure.

operations.description: Resolve the OS handle value for CRT handle index a1 via sub_595A1F(a1).
Guard: when sub_595A1F(a1) returns -1 (invalid handle), skip CloseHandle and treat the close as success.
Guard: when a1 is 1 or 2 (stdout/stderr) and sub_595A1F(2) equals sub_595A1F(1) (shared console handle), skip CloseHandle to avoid closing shared console output.
Invoke CloseHandle on the resolved OS handle; a success returns nonzero, so the error path is taken only when CloseHandle fails.
Set LastError = 0 when the handle was skipped or CloseHandle succeeded, otherwise LastError = GetLastError().
Invoke sub_5959A0(a1) to clean up the handle entry metadata after the close.
Clear the open-state byte for the handle: *(BYTE*)(dword_8D4920[a1>>5] + 36*(a1&0x1F) + 4) = 0.
On LastError nonzero, map the OS error to CRT errno via ErrorIDLookupTable(LastError) and return -1.
Called by sub_58C331 (0x0058C331) on the frame path to close a handle with errno mapping.

clean_pseudocode: else if ((a1 == 1 || a1 == 2) && sub_595A1F(2) == sub_595A1F(1)) { /* shared console, skip */ }
unresolved: Meaning of the block tracking array indexed by dword_8D4920[a1>>5] with 36-byte stride per handle slot is not proven here.
